The transit method and radial velocity method have indeed been the primary techniques responsible for the vast majority of confirmed exoplanet discoveries. The transit method, which detects the slight dimming of a star's light when a planet passes in front of it, has been particularly successful with missions like Kepler and TESS. The radial velocity method, which measures the wobble of a star caused by an orbiting planet's gravitational pull, was actually responsible for the first confirmed exoplanet discovery around a main-sequence star (51 Pegasi b in 1995). Together, these two methods have confirmed thousands of exoplanets, making Statement 1 accurate and Statement 2 completely incorrect.
